properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-17, thinking out loud: "I feel like there are some other design principles that while they are my own philosophies, should apply to anybody building with reflow2 ... I think they should be advisory guidelines for any reflow2 project (of course the user can waive them if they want)."

THE SOURCE: dev_storyflow's seven ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES, which he user-set over 2026-06-17 → 2026-07-04 and MIGRATED INTO A DESIGN GRAPH on 2026-08-09 as `rule:fleet_*` DesignRule nodes. Read from `origin/main` on 2026-08-17 (the local checkout was 289 commits behind; the pre-migration prose was recovered from the commit before `57f6bbb5`).

  1. Right long-term fix — no patches or stopgaps. TWO ORDERED STEPS: determine the actual root cause FIRST (reproduce, trace, prove the mechanism), THEN fix at the root cause. "A fix without an identified root cause is a guess."
  2. No silent fallbacks — fail loudly or STOP AND REPORT. "An INTEGRITY line, not a style preference."
  3. Done = end-to-end + lens-exposed. Merged is not done.
  4. Verify your OWN claims before posting; UI work must be observed live.
  5. Real-path tests — unit-green is not live-green.
  6. No silent caps or truncation — if you bounded coverage, SAY SO.
  7. Modular, maintainable code — no monoliths (+ Python DI / typing.Protocol / flat hierarchies).

⭐⭐ THE FINDING THAT REFRAMES THE WHOLE QUESTION, and it was not obvious until the seven were lined up: SIX OF THE SEVEN ARE ONE PRINCIPLE WEARING SEVEN COATS — the report must not overstate the work. A stopgap reports a fix that did not happen (1). A swallowed error reports success (2). "Merged" reported as "done" (3). An unverified claim posted as fact (4). Unit-green reported as live coverage (5). A truncated sweep reported as complete (6). Only #7 (modularity) is about structure rather than honesty.

⇒ THAT IS `epoch:instruments-stop-overstating`, ARRIVED AT FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION. reflow2 spent this whole increment building the same principle for its own reports; his fleet derived it from agents writing code. Two independent derivations of one idea is the strongest evidence available that it is not a house style. It also changes what shipping them would MEAN: not "reflow2 has opinions about your coding", but reflow2 extending its own core doctrine — report don't judge, a zero must say which zero — outward to the project being designed.

⇒ AND REFLOW2 ALREADY IMPLEMENTS THREE OF THEM ON ITSELF, which is either the best argument or a warning about scope: #6 IS `req:a-report-says-what-it-swept-and-whether-its-checks-ran`; #4 is `dec:three-party-checks` plus the standing "claims must be evidence-backed" rule; #1 is `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap` and `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause`, accepted hours before this conversation.

THE OPTIONS, none chosen:
(A) SEEDED AS NODES. `genesis` / `reflow2_init` writes them into every new graph as advisory DesignRules. Durable, queryable, waivable per project by editing the node. COST: seven nodes nobody in that project authored, in a tool whose pitch is that the graph holds YOUR design.
(B) SERVED AS A SKILL, like every other reflow2 skill — read on demand, nothing written. Zero footprint, always current with the server. COST: skills are advice to an agent; nothing records that a project adopted or waived one, so the waiver he wants has nowhere to live.
(C) BOTH — served as guidance, and OFFERED at genesis as a starter pack the user accepts, edits or declines. The acceptance is the user's word, so nothing is asserted on their behalf.
(D) NOT SHIPPED. Documented as a recommended starting set in the kit's prose, left for each project to adopt by hand.

⚠️ THE OBJECTION, recorded beside the idea rather than argued down, and it is his own doctrine turned on this: he holds that a VIEW must be a pure projection and that renderer fill-ins are reflow2 DEFECTS — content appearing in an output that nobody put in the design. Seven pre-seeded rules are arguably that same shape one layer up: graph content no one in the project authored. Option (C) is the shape that answers it, because the user's acceptance is what puts them there; (A) is the shape most exposed to it.

⚠️ AND THE UNIVERSALITY IS UNEVEN — see `dec:idea-a-principle-has-a-universal-core-and-local-clothes`.
⚠️ AND "ADVISORY" IS NOT A FREE DEFAULT — see `dec:idea-how-does-a-shipped-principle-say-whether-it-is-enforced`.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 ship a default set of advisory design principles to every project it is installed into?
properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming. The reframing is the contribution: six of the seven principles are the same principle — a report must not overstate the work — which is the epoch reflow2 has spent this increment building for its own instruments. That makes shipping them an extension of reflow2's existing doctrine rather than an importing of house style, and it is the strongest argument available for doing it at all.
